title: 5. Data Collection, Quality & Outliers
description: Assess data quality, detect anomalies, and handle outliers using the IQR method.

blocks.content:
### Assessing Data Quality & Detecting Outliers

An **outlier** is an observation that lies an abnormal distance from other values in a random sample. Outliers can skew model predictions significantly.

#### Interquartile Range (IQR) Method
- $Q1 = 25\text{th percentile}$
- $Q3 = 75\text{th percentile}$
- $IQR = Q3 - Q1$
- Lower Bound $= Q1 - 1.5 \times IQR$
- Upper Bound $= Q3 + 1.5 \times IQR$

![House Price Outliers Box Plot](/images/ml/chart_box_plot.png)

A model learns from the examples it sees, so messy or unfair examples teach messy or unfair patterns. Cleaning means checking values, labels, duplicates, and missing pieces.

More data is not automatically better. A smaller, relevant, carefully checked set can teach more than a huge pile of confusing examples.

blocks.starterCode:
from statistics import median

prices = [250, 270, 280, 300, 310, 320, 330, 340, 350, 950]
ordered = sorted(prices)
middle = median(ordered)
lower_half, upper_half = ordered[:5], ordered[5:]
q1, q3 = median(lower_half), median(upper_half)
iqr = q3 - q1
upper_bound = q3 + 1.5 * iqr
outliers = [price for price in prices if price > upper_bound]

print("Typical middle price:", middle)
print("Upper outlier boundary:", upper_bound)
print("Check these values:", outliers)

from statistics import median

prices = [250, 270, 280, 300, 310, 320, 330, 340, 350, 950]
ordered = sorted(prices)
middle = median(ordered)
lower_half, upper_half = ordered[:5], ordered[5:]
q1, q3 = median(lower_half), median(upper_half)
iqr = q3 - q1
upper_bound = q3 + 1.5 * iqr
outliers = [price for price in prices if price > upper_bound]

print("Typical middle price:", middle)
print("Upper outlier boundary:", upper_bound)
print("Check these values:", outliers)
